title: capacity-slot-rebalancer-proposal-and-oncall-runbook-draft
content:
Purpose and quick summary:
- Short: capture an on-call pattern we've seen repeatedly (midday p99 spikes tied to one tenant suddenly occupying many small slots), document temporary triage steps, and propose a 'slot rebalancer' mitigation + runbook.
- Motivation: recurring noisy-tenant-induced pool degradation that is not solved by eviction thresholds alone. Evictions are disruptive and have customer impact; if we can redistribution slots preemptively we lower p99 without evicting.

Observed pattern (recap from last three incidents):
- 12:10–12:45 local window, sustained step increase in pool p99 and 95th CPU/GPU scheduling latency.
- single tenant consumes ~60% of active small-slot allocations for ~15–30 minutes while their job bursts.
- autoscaler reacts slowly (scale-up event after 6–8m), causing backlog and queue latency.
- KV cache hit-rate drops (prefix caching degraded when many short-lived sessions appear).
- existing noisy-tenant signals (entropy metric, rapid slot-claim rate) often appear only after the client has already caused harm.

Immediate detection signals to add to alerting (alerts to tune now):
- rapid-slot-claim-rate > 250/min over 3m (new metric derived from allocator events).
- small-slot-occupancy-ratio per-tenant > 0.5 for >5m while pool_util > 0.7.
- queue_wait_seconds p99 > 3000ms AND pool_gpu_allocated_ratio > 0.85.
- kv_cache_hit_rate drop >= 15% over 2m.

Temporary on-call mitigation (playbook - quick steps):
1) Confirm: check Grafana dashboard ("slotting-overview") and allocator logs (kubectl -n dedicated logs deploy/allocator -f).
2) Identify tenant(s): run redis query: ZRANGE active-tenants 0 -1 WITHSCORES then cross-ref tenant->slot counts via Allocator API: GET /allocator/v1/tenants?sort=slots_desc
3) If a single tenant >50% small-slot occupancy AND causing p99 > target: throttle that tenant to a controlled qps cap via router policy (temporary route config):
   - curl -X POST https://controlplane/reconfigure -d '{"tenant":"T1234","qps_cap":20}'
   - note: this is disruptive; communicate to SE oncall.
4) If throttle is not acceptable, trigger manual slot reassign: use allocator tool to move N small slots off the tenant to fractional-eviction pool (non-evicting quarantine):
   - ./allocatorctl move-slots --from-tenant T1234 --count 12 --to-pool quarantine-small
   - watch for steady p99 drop in 2–5 minutes.
5) If autoscaler lagging, force a controlled scale-up: POST /autoscaler/force?pool=dedicated-small&scale_to=+2
6) After recovery, collect heap/profile logs from allocator (S3:/tmp/allocator-traces/<timestamp>) and tag ticket.

Notes to self (oncall commentary):
- Throttling is blunt but sometimes required for customer-facing SLAs. Prefer rebalancer over throttle if possible.
- Quarantine pool should have lower priority but not cause eviction; it's for graceful de-escalation.
- Need safe guard: do not move slots off a tenant if they have a pinned model version that only lives on specific hosts. Add check in allocatorctl.

Slot Rebalancer proposal (high level):
- Goal: dynamically rebalance small-slot allocations across tenants within a pool to reduce concentration and preempt noisy-tenant spikes.
- Inputs: per-tenant slot count, recent slot-claim-rate, seq_len_distribution, kv_cache_hit_rate, model_pin_count, migration_cost_estimate.
- Heuristic: if tenant_slot_fraction > 0.4 && slot_claim_rate > threshold_for_size => schedule proactive moves to reduce to 0.2 fraction, limited to X slots per minute to avoid thundering herd.
- Safety checks: avoid moving if model_pin_count > 0 and those hosts are the only place for that model; check network IO cost estimate.
- Rate limits: global max migrations per pool = 3/min; per-tenant max migrations = 1/min; abort if migrations_pending > 5.

Operator runbook (draft short form) - when rebalancer exists:
1) Alert fires: "ConcentrationAttack:small-slot-fraction"
2) Oncall runs quick triage: confirm pools affected, tenants above fraction, recent migrations.
3) Hit 'preview' endpoint: GET /allocator/rebalancer/preview?tenant=T1234 => shows candidate moves and cost estimate.
4) If preview looks safe, POST /allocator/rebalancer/execute?dry_run=false.
5) Observe: timeline should show gradual p99 decline; if p99 unchanged after 10m, rollback via POST /allocator/rebalancer/rollback?op=<id>.
6) If migration causes unexpected failures (OOMs, driver errors), immediately rollback and raise P0 incident.

Telemetry / query primitives to add (PromQL suggestions):
- slot_claim_rate = rate(allocator_slot_claims_total[1m])
- tenant_slot_fraction = allocator_slots_by_tenant / sum(allocator_slots_by_tenant) (per-tenant)
- migration_pending = allocator_migrations_in_progress{pool="dedicated-small"}

Experiment log (mini notes from last run):
- 2026-01-18 experiment: rebalancer alpha ran against canary pool for 48h. Results: mean p99 down 12%, p95 down 7%, but two customers saw increased session setup time (~+300ms) because migrations invalidated cold KV caches.
- Learned: add migration warmup: replicate prefix caches for moving slots prior to cutover. Also throttle migrations to avoid sequential cache invalidations.

Open questions / risks:
- Are we allowed to move slots between hosts that cross EBS volumes? snapshot/quiesce cost unknown. Legal/PCI tenants might disallow cross-host moves. Need ACL check.
- How to quantify migration cost vs eviction cost cleanly? Need benchmark.
- Will rebalancer interact poorly with autoscaler hysteresis? Need simulation.

Follow-ups / action items (owners & ETA):
- (Diego) implement preview endpoint + safe-checks in allocatorctl - ETA 2026-03-05.
- (Anika) add alert for rapid-slot-claim-rate and tenant_slot_fraction - ETA 2026-02-28.
- (Liam) run migration cost benchmark (cold vs warmed caches) and publish numbers to Confluence - ETA 2026-03-12.
- (Maya) draft communication template for SE to use when throttling tenants - ETA 2026-02-25.
- (SRE) schedule chaos test simulating 10 concurrent small-slot migrations during peak - ETA 2026-03-20.

Post-incident notes (for retrospective):
- Do not rely solely on autoscaler to fix concentration issues; scale-up is necessary but often too late.
- Eviction thresholds are necessary but user-impacting. Rebalancer + quarantine is less user-visible.
- We need a policy table mapping tenant tiers -> allowed migration cross-host, allowed throttle windows, compliance flags.

Raw links / tickets / snippets to copy into incident ticket:
- Allocator logs: s3://redwood-logs/allocator/2026-02-11/alloc-20260211-1205.log
- Ticket: JIRA RED-4621 (incident capture)
- PR with naive rebalancer prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/234
- Slack thread: #sre-dedicated-incident (ts: 2026-02-11 12:18 UTC)

Quick checklist for oncall (TL;DR):
- Open Grafana -> slotting-overview.
- Run allocatorctl top-tenants. Identify concentration.
- If concentration >50% -> preview rebalancer moves.
- If safe -> execute rebalancer. If not safe -> apply throttle -> force scale-up -> contact SE.
- After stabilization -> attach logs to JIRA and kick off postmortem if customer impact > P2.

Notes-toward-final-runbook: this doc will be iterative. Next revision should include concrete CLI ergonomics, RBAC flows, and a small-state machine diagram for the rebalancer decisions. Also need legal/enterprise flagging earlier in the flow.

Unpolished bits / TODO in doc:
- Add example allocatorctl commands for preview/execute/rollback (CLI args).
- Add PromQL exact queries and alert thresholds as code blocks.
- Add a short customer-facing note template.

End of draft.
